correctness.rationale: For every nontrivial character of the closed image subgroup, composition with the compact-group homomorphism is a nontrivial unimodular completely multiplicative scalar function. Multiplicative pseudorandomness and the focal paper's Lemma 2.1 force the corresponding Fourier coefficient of the auxiliary measures to vanish in the same iterated limit used in Theorem 6.1. Character density then gives convergence against continuous test functions to Haar measure. The focal paper's equation (6.3) removes finite initial segments, so every nonempty open set is hit at arbitrarily large indices. The reverse inclusion is immediate. The Piatetski--Shapiro and nil-Bohr corollaries use Theorems 1.3 and 1.4 exactly as stated.

value.rationale: The result closes a structural gap between scalar value distribution and simultaneous recurrence: it determines exactly which joint targets are attainable, including the constraints imposed by algebraic relations among coordinates. It yields immediate joint-limit theorems for the newly established Piatetski--Shapiro and nil-Bohr pseudorandom families and separates qualitative joint density from the stronger, still-unproved multivariate equidistribution problem.
